narrative.overview: The page is one job told in three coats: Primer, Base, Finish. A pinned stage holds three full-bleed panels (pale primer grey, royal blue, deep navy). Each next coat rises over the last through a liquid, dripping SVG edge as you scroll, with a thin white highlight line riding the edge. Around it the site is calm deep navy with silver type, so the real before/after photographs and the 3D logo carry the color.
keyCharacteristics: Navy-first dark ground; royal blue is the single action color; silver is the neutral voice.
Liquid wavy coat edges (SVG clipPath plus highlight stroke) are the signature device.
Photos are white-matted prints, slightly rotated, drifting at different scroll speeds.
Pill-shaped controls, generously rounded photo frames, no sharp corners on interactive things.
Sound (drip, whoosh, scrape, pop) is part of the interaction grammar and is user-toggleable.

rules.name: The Logo Palette Rule
rules.body: Every color traces back to the logo: navy, silver/chrome, royal blue. A new hue needs a reason in the logo.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Royal blue (or silver on the blue-adjacent Finish panel) marks the one primary action. On the royal-blue coat the button flips to silver so it never disappears into its ground.

rules.name: The Wide-Over-Quiet Rule
rules.body: Only Unbounded carries emphasis; Albert Sans never goes display-size.

rules.name: The Print Only Rule
rules.body: Shadow belongs to photographs lying on a coat. Buttons, cards and bands stay flat.

dos: Do keep one primary action per coat and per band, in royal blue (silver on the blue coat).
Do lay real photographs as white-matted, slightly rotated prints and label them honestly with the stage they show.
Do shape any new coat or section boundary as a liquid, dripping edge with a thin white highlight.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: no blobs, no edge wobble.
Do keep tap targets at 44px minimum and focus outlines visible.
donts: Don't introduce hues outside navy, royal blue, silver and primer grey.
Don't add shadows to anything but photographs.
Don't use Unbounded below title size for running text, or Albert Sans for display.
Don't use straight, hard section cuts inside the coat sequence.
